title: Your mosque

cards: Friday, a little after noon. Outside a door, shoes pile up in crooked rows: work boots, sneakers, a toddler's sandals, polished office shoes.

Inside, a man who fixes cars stands next to a man who teaches at the university, and neither one is thinking about that. A taxi driver slips into the back row. Somebody's grandmother is already in her usual spot.
For a few minutes, nobody is anyone's boss. Then the row straightens, and they bow together. Day one hundred thirty-seven asked what a mosque is.
Today, what it's like to belong to one.

teach.h: THE CALL ON THE DAY OF CONGREGATION.
teach.b: Start with the call. Surah al-Jumu'ah says, in Pickthall's words: "O ye who believe! When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading."

In the Sunni schools of law the Friday prayer, with its sermon, is required of adult men who are settled in a place, and women may attend; when they do, it takes the place of the noon prayer. Why together?
In Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says prayer in congregation is twenty-seven degrees better than prayer alone. Twenty-seven is the hadith's own number.
The point underneath is simple: the same prayer, said shoulder to shoulder, isn't the same experience. Who gets to come?

teach.h: DON'T STOP THE WOMEN FROM THE MOSQUES.
teach.b: In another hadith in Bukhari, the Prophet says not to stop the women servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah.
Mosques today arrange space for women in different ways, and Muslims discuss openly how well that's working.
And what belonging asks. A mosque isn't a perfect place. The sermon may run long; the parking may be a mess; someone may be rude about where you stood.
Belonging isn't the same as liking everything. It means you're known by face, you notice when someone is missing, and somebody notices when you are.
That's a lot to ask of a building, and it's exactly what people go back for.

how: On Friday around midday, Muslims gather at the mosque for Jumu'ah: a sermon from the imam followed by a congregational prayer, which is required of adult resident men and open to women, and which takes the place of the noon prayer for those who attend.

o: a place where the row lines up and you are known, and missed
any room where Muslims eat together after Friday prayer
a building only scholars may enter to lead the prayers

p: not to be stopped from the mosques

games.q: it's Friday. you're in the middle of a sale when you hear the call to the Friday prayer. what does surah al-Jumu'ah say?
o: haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading.
finish the sale, then think about it.
games.why: "haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading" (62:9). the next verse says that once the prayer is ended, people may go out and seek Allah's bounty again.

practice: Think of a place where you're known by face, a mosque, a team, a building where someone waves, and let rise the name of someone who would notice if you didn't come, then the name of someone who has stopped turning up.

If you pray, ask Allah to keep them well; if you don't, simply hold them in mind. If you're Muslim and able, you might plan to go this Friday a little early; if you aren't Muslim, some mosques welcome visitors.

wordCard.voice: Your mosque. The place where the row straightens on Friday, and where you are known, and missed. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Friday, the day of congregation.

carryVoice: Your line: belong somewhere. Known by face, and missed on the Fridays you're gone. Until tomorrow.
